patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, PAD and CAD after a 2016 MI and stent, who joins in 2021. New exertional angina in 2024 leads to a stress test, catheterization showing three-vessel disease, and CABG in September 2025; a right total knee arthroplasty follows in July 2026 after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
61M here to set up primary care. Wants a practice where he can reach the doctor directly; a friend from the cafe he walks to every morning sent him our way.

HPI: Long-standing type 2 diabetes on metformin, blood pressure on lisinopril, cholesterol on atorvastatin. Heart attack in 2016, had a stent put in at that time, and has seen an outside cardiology group roughly once a year since; he thinks his next visit there is summer 2023 but is not sure. Takes a baby aspirin every day since the MI. Gets cramping in both calves after walking a few blocks, eases when he stands a minute; has had that a couple of years and was told it is circulation. Right knee aches with stairs and long days; takes Tylenol when it acts up, avoids anti-inflammatories because the cardiologist told him to. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no palpitations, no fainting. No bleeding.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, CAD s/p MI with stent 2016, PAD with claudication, right knee OA.
PSH: coronary stent 2016.
Meds: aspirin 81 daily; metformin 1000 BID; lisinopril 20 daily; atorvastatin 40 daily; metoprolol succinate 50 daily; acetaminophen 500 1-2 tabs prn.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father had a heart attack at 68 and heart surgery around then; mother type 2 diabetes; brother has coronary disease.
SH: retired construction foreman, ran job sites for years. Smoked about a pack a day for close to 30 years, stopped in 2013. Does not drink. Up early, oatmeal, reads the paper, walks to the cafe to see friends. Plays chess. Has grandchildren nearby.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Comfortable, talkative. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: warm, skin intact, no ulcers; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses diminished both sides; monofilament sensation intact. Right knee: crepitus, no effusion, full extension, flexion to about 110.

A/P:
1. T2DM: A1c today. Metformin continued. Needs eye exam - he goes to an optometrist in town, will ask them to send the report.
2. HTN: 134/80 today, continue lisinopril and metoprolol. CMP.
3. CAD s/p MI/stent, hyperlipidemia: lipids today; continue atorvastatin 40, aspirin, metoprolol. Will get cardiology notes.
4. PAD: claudication stable, encouraged walking program as tolerated.
5. R knee OA: acetaminophen as needed, ok to continue.
6. Former smoker, 30 pk-yr, quit 8 yrs ago: eligible for yearly low-dose CT; ordered, he is agreeable.
7. HM: HCV and HIV screen once today, PHQ-2 negative. Colonoscopy 2019 per patient, records requested. Vaccines - will look at records; flu and pneumococcal in the fall.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Charles, good to meet you on Tuesday. Your labs are back. The A1c, which reflects average sugar over about three months, is 6.9 - right about where we want it. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal and there is no protein leaking into the urine. Cholesterol numbers look reasonable on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes to your medicines. The radiology office will call to schedule the lung CT.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 23 pages, from the patient's former primary care office (seen there 2014-2021).

Contents reviewed and summarized:
- Problem list: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, CAD with MI 2016 treated with a coronary stent, PAD, right knee osteoarthritis.
- 2016 hospital summary (abstracted): presented with chest pain, myocardial infarction, coronary stent placed, discharged on aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol and lisinopril.
- Screening colonoscopy, 2019: normal to the cecum, no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Medication list matches what the patient brought in.
- Allergies: NKDA.

Scanned to chart. Routed to PCP for review.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening, former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2013. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal; coronary artery calcification is present. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative screening CT, no nodules. Coronary calcification expected given his known CAD. Repeat in one year. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: requesting 90-day supplies of metformin 1000, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 and metoprolol succinate 50 under new prescriber. Pt on all per med list. Sent per protocol, 90 days with 3 refills each.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for vaccines. Afebrile, feels well, no prior vaccine reactions. VIS given for each. Flu (quadrivalent) L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid, Shingrix dose 1 L deltoid lower site. Tolerated, waited 15 min, no reaction. Told him the Shingrix can make the arm sore and him tired for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months, will give at his December visit.

Optometry report

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Doing fine. Walking most mornings, still gets the calf cramps at about the same distance, no worse. Knee grumbles in the cold. No chest discomfort, no shortness of breath with his usual activity. Taking everything, no missed doses. Eye exam done in October, no retinopathy.

O: BP and pulse in vitals. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. No ankle swelling. Feet intact, pulses faint at both ankles as before.

A/P:
- DM2: A1c drawn today. Metformin same.
- HTN: at goal, no change.
- CAD/HLD: stable, no angina. Continue regimen.
- PAD: stable claudication.
- Shingrix #2 given today, series complete.
Physical in June with fasting labs.

documents.title: A1c and BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.0, BMP normal. Message to pt: steady, no change.

documents.title: Physical appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I need to book my yearly physical for June and want to know if I should come in without breakfast for the blood work. Also my metformin bottle says no refills left. Thanks, Charlie Leblanc

documents.title: RE: Physical appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Leblanc, you are booked for Tuesday June 14 at 8:40. Yes, please skip breakfast that morning - water and your morning pills are fine. I checked with the nurse and your metformin had refills sent in August; the pharmacy may have it under the old prescription. Call us back if they can't find it.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62 y/o man for yearly exam, fasting.

Interval: no ER visits, no new problems. Babysits the grandkids two afternoons a week now, which he says keeps him moving. Same calf tightness after several blocks. Right knee about the same; Tylenol a few times a week. No chest pain or pressure, no dyspnea, no orthopnea, no bruising beyond the odd mark on his forearms. Bowels regular, no blood. Urinary stream ok, gets up once at night.

Meds reviewed: aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: Well appearing. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck without thyromegaly or bruit. RRR, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender, no bruit, no mass. No edema. Feet: no lesions, sensation normal to monofilament, DP/PT pulses diminished bilaterally. Skin: a few small ecchymoses on the forearms. Mood bright.

Plan:
- Fasting labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin.
- Tdap today (last one he can't remember).
- Lung CT due July, ordered.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal - next 2029.
- Eye exam fall, he will schedule.
- Continue all meds. Diabetes check in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.0, LDL 80, kidney and liver normal, CBC normal, urine microalbumin normal. Portal: all good, keep going.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual lung cancer screening. Comparison 2021-07-20. Low-dose noncontrast technique. No lung nodule identified. No emphysematous change of note. Lungs otherwise clear without consolidation. No pleural effusion. Coronary artery calcification and stent material are noted. Mediastinum normal. Bones without suspicious lesion.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L arm, bivalent COVID booster R arm. Screening questions negative. Observed 15 minutes, left feeling fine. Had his original COVID series and a booster elsewhere in 2021 - card shown, outside doses entered from card.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry - diabetic eye evaluation
Date of exam: 2022-11-01
Dilated exam both eyes. Retina: no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization. Maculae flat. Optic nerves healthy, cup-to-disc 0.3 both eyes.
Assessment: diabetes mellitus without retinopathy.
Plan: annual dilated exam. New reading glasses prescribed.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Charles is in for diabetes and BP. Nothing new. Holiday baking is the main threat to his sugars, he says. No hypoglycemia symptoms. No chest symptoms. Calves same. Knee same.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Ankles without swelling.

Plan: A1c and BMP. Same medicines. Refills current. See him for the physical in May; cardiology yearly visit is due next summer - he has their number.
